title: React Module 05 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of state, events, useState, immutable updates, batching, stale closures, and lifting state up.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Data a component remembers between renders
A prop that children must mutate

questions.explanation: State is data owned by a component that React remembers and uses to render.

options.text: An array with the current value and a setter function
A promise that resolves after render

questions.explanation: `useState` returns `[state, setState]`, usually named for the value being stored.

questions.prompt: Changing a regular local variable in a component automatically causes React to re-render.
questions.explanation: Local variables are recalculated on render and changing them does not schedule a render. State setters do.

questions.prompt: Which event prop handles a button click in React?
questions.explanation: React event props use camelCase names such as `onClick`.

questions.prompt: Which values often belong in state? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Values that change over time and affect rendering
Data that can be directly derived from existing props every render

questions.explanation: State is for changing values that affect UI. Derived values often do not need separate state.

questions.prompt: Which update correctly treats an object state value immutably?
questions.explanation: Create a new object instead of mutating the existing state object.

questions.prompt: When should you use a functional state update like `setCount(c => c + 1)`?

options.text: When the next state depends on the previous state

questions.explanation: Functional updates read the latest queued previous value, avoiding stale state issues.

questions.prompt: Which statements about lifting state up are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Move shared state to the nearest common parent
Pass current values down as props
Pass callbacks down for children to request changes
Duplicate the same state independently in every child

questions.explanation: Lifting state creates one source of truth that children use through props and callbacks.
